steps.title: Two endpoints
steps.text: `POST /links` takes a long URL and returns a 7-character code. `GET /<code>` answers with a 301 redirect. Nothing else is in scope for the first version.
steps.narration: The service does two things: create a short code and redirect from it.

steps.title: Where links are stored
steps.text: Each link is one row: `code`, `target_url`, `created_at`, `owner_id`. Reads outnumber writes about 100 to 1, and the row count stays under 50 million for the next two years.
steps.narration: Links need a durable store. The data is small and read-heavy.

interaction.prompt: Which database holds the links table?

options.label: Postgres
options.pros: Unique constraint on code, team already runs it

options.label: DynamoDB
options.pros: No capacity planning, key lookups only
options.cons: New to the team, harder local dev

steps.title: How codes are generated
steps.text: A code must be unique and hard to guess in sequence. With 62 characters and length 7 there are about 3.5 trillion codes, so collisions stay rare.
steps.narration: Pick between random codes with a retry, or codes derived from a counter.

steps.title: Caching redirects
steps.text: Most traffic hits a few hundred popular codes. A cache in front of Postgres keeps redirect latency under 5 ms and takes read load off the primary.
steps.narration: A cache serves the hot codes so Postgres only sees misses.

options.label: Redis, shared
options.pros: All API instances share hits, TTL per key

options.label: In-process LRU
options.pros: No network hop, nothing to deploy
options.cons: Each instance warms its own cache

options.label: No cache yet
options.cons: Every redirect is a database read

steps.title: Counting clicks off the hot path
steps.text: The redirect handler appends a click event to a Redis stream and returns. A worker reads the stream and inserts counts in batches every 10 seconds.
steps.narration: Click counting happens asynchronously, so redirects never wait on analytics.

steps.title: Open questions
steps.text: Not decided yet: whether links expire, how owners delete a link, and whether we block known phishing domains at creation time.
steps.narration: Three questions are still open. Add anything else that should be settled first.
